tech.name: ChatGPT Wallet (agent payments with card-network tokens, in dots)
tech.status: shipped, limited rollout: ChatGPT Pro subscribers 18+ in the US with eligible US-issued cards
tech.one_line: You approve each purchase with Face ID or a fingerprint; the card network issues a payment token (its own number, code and expiry) so your dot pays without the agent or the business seeing your real card.

predecessor.name: ChatGPT agent (2025): asked before a purchase; you took over its browser and typed your real card

hook.text: ChatGPT Wallet: before, you'd stop, type your card; now 1 scan, it pays, never seeing your 3 numbers, but how, why, in 60 seconds?

claims.text: ChatGPT agent asks your permission before a purchase.
For sensitive inputs you use takeover mode and type into the agent's browser yourself.
Each Wallet purchase is approved with one security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan.
The payment token replaces the three card details (card number, security code, expiration date), and Wallet does not share the actual card details with the business or agent.

before.text: Here's how, in one errand: you send a helper to the shop. Before, ChatGPT's agent stopped at checkout. You took over its browser, typed your real card, and the shop got all three numbers.

claims.text: ChatGPT agent (launched July 17, 2025) explicitly asks for your permission before actions with real-world consequences, like making a purchase.
Use takeover mode for sensitive inputs: you take control of the agent's virtual browser and type yourself.
Typing a card into a checkout gives the business the actual card details; Wallet's contrast is that it does not share them with the business or agent.

new.text: Now, since November 13, your dot carries a wallet. At checkout it shows you the items, the total and the card. You approve with Face ID or a fingerprint. Then the card network hands over a stand-in: its own number, code and date.

claims.text: ChatGPT Wallet was introduced on November 13, 2026, and launches in dots.
Before each purchase, the user reviews the items, total, and selected card.
The user approves with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan.
After approval, the payment network provides a payment token, a substitute for the actual card details, with a card number, security code, and expiration date.
The token is a substitute card number with its own security code and expiration date.

why.text: The shop charges the stand-in; the bill lands on your real card, rewards and all. Your agent never sees your card, and neither does the shop.

claims.text: The charge goes to the user's selected card without Wallet sharing the actual card details with the business or agent.
Users keep their card's existing rewards and protections for eligible disputes.

takeaway.text: How? One scan, then a stand-in card. Why? Your three numbers stay out of the errand. For now, only Pro users in America, and some shops may block it. Your helper still runs the errand; it just never holds your wallet.

claims.text: Initially available to ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and older in the US with eligible US-issued cards.
Some sites may unintentionally block purchases through ChatGPT Wallet.

background.text: Built with American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa; merchants are asked to recognise signed agent requests (Web Bot Auth) and work with risk partners; risk systems may still flag legitimate agent purchases.
OpenAI built it with American Express, Mastercard and Visa; retailers must separate wanted bots from unwanted ones.
Instant Checkout (2025) used encrypted payment tokens at participating merchants only (Etsy sellers first).
Visa announced its payment network inside ChatGPT on June 10, 2026 (press).
